_comment: Example operator config for the legal pages. Copy this file to your deployment directory (NOT into the public repo!) as 'operator.json' and fill in your real values. It is intentionally NOT covered by the signed manifest: it is deployment-specific data. Only strings; no HTML or code. Legal placeholders contain example text for an Italian operator and MUST be adapted to your jurisdiction, including NIS2 classification, DSA registration, and other regulatory obligations. This is NOT legal advice.
OPERATOR_DPA_NAME: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
OPERATOR_HOSTING_NOTE: The hosting VM is located in the European Economic Area; no international transfer applies.
OPERATOR_LOG_RETENTION: The application and its reverse proxy are configured not to retain persistent access logs. No IP addresses, User-Agent strings, or request metadata are written to disk. IP addresses may be held transiently in server memory during active connections for rate limiting and abuse prevention, then discarded.
OPERATOR_HOSTING_PROVIDER_LOG_NOTE: The hosting provider may independently retain infrastructure-level network logs (e.g., netflow, connection metadata) in accordance with its own policies; such processing is outside the Operator's direct control.
OPERATOR_LIABILITY_LOCAL_LAW_NOTE: This limitation applies to the fullest extent permitted under Italian law, including Articles 1218 and 1229 of the Italian Civil Code.
OPERATOR_DPO_NOTE: Based on the current scale and nature of this Service, no Data Protection Officer is believed to be required under Article 37 GDPR. This assessment will be reviewed if the Service's scope or data processing activities change materially.
OPERATOR_LEGAL_CLASSIFICATION_NOTE: The Service constitutes a number-independent interpersonal communications service (NI-ICS) within the meaning of the applicable electronic communications framework. It is not subject to a general authorisation requirement. The Operator cooperates with competent judicial authorities to the extent technically feasible given the data actually held at the time of the request.
OPERATOR_LEGAL_FRAMEWORK_NOTE: PinChat is a number-independent interpersonal communications service (NI-ICS) within the meaning of Article 2(hhh) of the Italian Electronic Communications Code (D.Lgs. 259/2003, as amended by D.Lgs. 207/2021 and D.Lgs. 48/2024). As an NI-ICS, the Service is exempt from the general authorisation requirement (Art. 11(2) CCE) and falls within the subjective scope of Art. 3, second sentence, of the Ministerial Decree of 28 December 2017 (implementing Art. 57(1) CCE). The Service is not subject to lawful interception obligations under Art. 57(2) CCE, which apply only to entities holding a general authorisation, nor to cyber-threat monitoring obligations under Art. 57(4) CCE (same prerequisite). The Service is excluded from the definition of 'online platform' under the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, recital 14) but falls within the scope of intermediary services as a 'mere conduit' (Art. 3(g)(i) DSA, recital 29) with reduced obligations and the protection of Art. 8 DSA (no general monitoring obligation). No general obligation exists under Italian law for a non-telecom, non-ISP service operator to routinely retain web access logs. The Provvedimento Amministratori di Sistema (Garante, 27/11/2008) does not apply in the case of a sole operator who is also the only system administrator. The data retention obligations under Art. 132 of the Codice Privacy (D.Lgs. 196/2003) apply to providers that possess traffic data and subscriber information; the Service generates neither by design. This does not mean that log retention would be unlawful — rather, for this specific deployment, no legitimate proportionate purpose has been identified that would outweigh the data minimisation principle.
OPERATOR_JUDICIAL_COOPERATION_NOTE: The Operator cooperates fully with the Italian judicial authorities and national security agencies within the limits of the data actually held. The encryption is end-to-end between users, with symmetric keys that never transit through the server (they are shared exclusively via the URL fragment, which by design is not sent to the server). In response to judicial requests, the Operator is technically able to confirm the existence of the Service and its management structure, but cannot provide communication content or identifying metadata, as such data are not generated or retained.
OPERATOR_CASE_LAW_NOTE: Italian case law has recognised that, in true end-to-end encrypted systems, encryption keys may be stored exclusively on the communicating devices, with the result that the service provider is structurally unable to access encryption keys or communication content. See Cass. pen., Sez. I, judgment no. 6363, filed 15 February 2023, and the additional Sez. I decision no. 19082, filed 5 May 2023, both in the Sky ECC litigation; and the subsequent Sezioni Unite judgments no. 23755 and no. 23756, hearing 29 February 2024, filed 14 June 2024. Those decisions concerned encrypted data obtained through foreign investigative action against infrastructure and later shared with Italy through judicial-cooperation channels (European Investigation Orders). The Sezioni Unite classified such data under the regime of evidence circulation between proceedings (Arts. 238 and 270 of the Code of Criminal Procedure), expressly excluding the applicability of Art. 234-bis.
OPERATOR_LEGAL_RISKS_NOTE: The Italian Ministerial Decree of 28 December 2017 does not contain a clause explicitly requiring cooperation regardless of encryption techniques adopted by the operator. Art. 4(1)(a) refers to 'regardless of the network technology employed or the type of access network', which concerns network-type neutrality (fixed, mobile, fibre), not encryption. Italian law does not currently contain an explicit obligation to decrypt communications or provide encryption keys to authorities, either at primary legislation level or in implementing decrees. Italian case law concerning Sky ECC (Cass. pen., Sez. I, judgment no. 6363, filed 15 February 2023; Sezioni Unite judgments no. 23755 and no. 23756, hearing 29 February 2024, filed 14 June 2024) has recognised that in true end-to-end encrypted systems, the service provider is structurally unable to access encryption keys or communication content. In those cases, encrypted data was obtained through foreign investigative operations against the infrastructure, not through an order to the provider to decrypt. A future Ministerial Decree under Art. 57(6) CCE, as amended by Legislative Decree no. 48/2024, could introduce architectural capability obligations (requiring providers to be technically able to intercept). No such decree currently exists for NI-ICS/OTT services. At EU level, the Child Sexual Abuse Regulation (CSAR / 'Chat Control 2.0', proposal 2022/0155(COD)) is in trilogue as of April 2026, with sessions scheduled for May and June 2026 and a political deal targeted for mid-2026. The proposal could impose scanning obligations on E2EE services. The interim ePrivacy derogation for voluntary scanning (Reg. 2021/1232, 'Chat Control 1.0') expired on 3 April 2026 after the European Parliament voted 311-228 to reject its extension. The ePrivacy framework remains under revision; nothing currently in force requires breaking E2EE.
OPERATOR_NIS2_NOTE: As a provider of electronic communications services accessible to the public, the Service falls within the size-independent scope of the NIS2 Directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2555), as transposed by Legislative Decree no. 138/2024, Art. 3(5)(b). The Operator is classified as an 'important entity' (not 'essential', as it does not meet the medium-enterprise threshold). The Operator has registered on the ACN (Agenzia per la Cybersicurezza Nazionale) platform and adopts security measures proportionate to the risks posed to the security of its network and information systems, including: HTTPS/TLS transport security, end-to-end encryption of all communication content (which is itself a conformity measure under Art. 21(2)(h) NIS2), Argon2id password hashing, HMAC-signed CSRF tokens, proof-of-work abuse mitigation, automatic room expiry, containerised deployment with non-root privileges and dropped Linux capabilities. The Operator will notify the CSIRT Italia of any significant incident in accordance with the applicable timelines.
OPERATOR_DSA_NOTE: The Service is classified as an intermediary service of the 'mere conduit' type under the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, Art. 3(g)(i), recital 29). As such, it benefits from the liability exemption under Art. 4 DSA and from the prohibition of general monitoring obligations under Art. 8 DSA. The Operator complies with the applicable obligations for intermediary services: designation of a point of contact for authorities (Art. 11 DSA), designation of a point of contact for recipients of the service (Art. 12 DSA), and publication of transparent terms and conditions (Art. 14 DSA). The Service is exempt from the transparency reporting obligation under Art. 15(2) DSA as it qualifies as a micro or small enterprise within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC.
